chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from 'Imran ibn Musa, from Musa ibn Ja'far, from 'Amr ibn Sa'id al-Madani, from Muhammad ibn 'Umar al-Sabbati, who said:
I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who bequeathed to me and instructed me to give something to his uncle every year, so the uncle died, and he wrote, 'Give it to his heirs.'
ai.seo_question: What happens to an annual bequest when the specific beneficiary dies?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the bequest to the uncle is a personal obligation tied to his life, so upon his death, the payment transfers to his heirs rather than terminating, illustrating the principle of *istidlal* (inference) from the phrase 'give to his heirs.' This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on interpreting the testator's intent (*niyyah*) to ensure the continuity of the bequest (*wasiyyah*) for the beneficiary's lineage. It serves as a key precedent in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* for distinguishing between bequests that are strictly personal and those that can be inherited.
